bib.title: Block Diffusion: Interpolating Between Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models

read.skipped: Appendix A/B derivations and sample text skimmed; references skimmed.

question: Can a language model interpolate between autoregressive and discrete diffusion to get arbitrary-length generation, KV caching and better perplexity than prior diffusion models?
hypothesis: Gradient variance is a key contributor to the perplexity gap between diffusion and AR models; data-driven clipped noise schedules reduce it.
contributions: Block discrete diffusion LMs: autoregressive over blocks, discrete diffusion within each block; variable length and KV caching.
Custom training algorithms using the whole batch of tokens (vectorized, single forward pass).
Identify gradient variance as limiting factor and propose data-driven clipped noise schedules.
New state-of-the-art perplexity among discrete diffusion models.

method.summary: Block diffusion LM: sequence split into blocks of L' tokens; p(x)=prod over blocks of a masked-diffusion conditional given previous blocks, parameterised by one transformer with block-causal attention over noisy+clean concatenation. A base model is pretrained with L'=L then finetuned per block size with a learned clipped mask-rate range.

datasets.name: LM1B
datasets.preprocessing: bert-base-uncased tokenizer, context 128, sequences concatenated and wrapped to 128 (not padded)

datasets.name: OpenWebText
datasets.split: last 100k documents held out for validation
datasets.preprocessing: GPT2 tokenizer, context 1024, concatenated and wrapped; no BOS/EOS injected

datasets.name: PTB, Wikitext, Lambada, AG News, Pubmed, Arxiv
datasets.preprocessing: sequences wrapped to 1024, no EOS between

models.name: BD3-LM
models.architecture: diffusion transformer with rotary embeddings, block-causal attention, no timestep conditioning
models.init_from: base BD3-LM pretrained with L'=L (850K steps) then finetuned

models.name: AR, SEDD, MDLM
models.architecture: same transformer as Sahoo et al. 2024a

other.note: retrained with wrapping (and without BOS/EOS on OWT) for fairness

training.objective: masked-diffusion NELBO per block (Eq 8) with clipped mask-rate schedule 1-alpha_t ~ U[beta,omega]

other.schedule search: grid search over beta, omega every validation epoch (~5K updates) minimising Var of NELBO

inference.decoding: block-wise diffusion sampling with KV cache; first-hitting sampler, 64-bit Gumbel; MDLM block-wise decoding with stride 512 for L=2048
inference.max_tokens: until EOS or mean entropy of last 256-token chunk < 4

parameters.T: 5K diffusion steps (BD3-LM, MDLM); 1K (SSD-LM, SEDD); 25 for SSD-LM matched-NFE

metrics.name: Test perplexity
metrics.definition: exp of NELBO per token under uniformly sampled mask rates; upper bound for diffusion

metrics.name: Var NELBO
metrics.definition: variance of NELBO estimator across batches and t

eval.protocol: Single Monte Carlo estimate of t with low-discrepancy sampler; no seeds or significance tests stated; low-entropy samples regenerated for Gen PPL.

limits: Training BD3-LMs is more expensive than regular diffusion training; vectorized algorithm keeps it within <2x of diffusion training speed.
Blocks are generated sequentially so may share the speed and controllability constraints of AR when blocks are small; optimal block size is task specific.
Still behind AR in perplexity (OWT 20.73 vs 17.54 best).
Only 110M-parameter models; no seeds or variance across runs reported; no wall-clock inference benchmark.
